# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ • Although we still believe that global economic worries are essentially positive for the gold price, news of a downgrade to Italian credit ratings and the US Federal Reserve’s decision not to start a third round of quantitative easing drove widespread selling throughout many asset markets. Gold was not immune and the price tumbled from $1,800 to a brief low of $1,550. For some investors, this should be a buying opportunity but, with margins being increased on COMEX and on the Shanghai Gold Exchange, excess bravery was in short supply. As the gold price fell, silver and the platinum group metals were dragged lower. Silver lost a third of its value in this two day slump. Palladium retraced its steps to levels last seen in October 2010. Platinum suffered too with risk aversion widening the differential with gold even as gold fell. Given production costs within South Africa, these current platinum prices are not sustainable in the longer term. However, in the shorter term, the price direction for these three more industrial precious metals will be driven by the tussle between soft economic output and worries over credit and banking risk. • With prices falling and the economic outlook worsening, it was no surprise to see net long speculative positioning on the futures exchanges declining for all four precious metals in the week to the 20th of September. Given margin increases on the gold and silver contracts in Shanghai and New York and extraordinary price falls since then, expect the next COTR report to indicate that substantial further selling has since taken place. • The week to the 23rd of September saw net selling in the Exchange Traded Funds for all four metals amongst a sea of red. With prices falling sharply, some investors were encouraged to book profits or forced to cut losses. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **26 September 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **26 September 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 20 September 2011; ETF data to 23 September 2011.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

In Euro terms, gold suffered less, finding support from this increasingly flimsy currency. However, the real action came in the middle of last week with gold slipping an unprecedented $260 in three days from $1,815 on the 21st to bounce off a low of roughly $1,550 on the 26th. On the 20th, credit ratings were cut for Italy and a number of Italian and American banks. Gold found a little riskbased support. On t eh 21st, the Federal Reserve revealed that it would embark on Operation Twist instead of QE3. The markets were unimpressed and simply collapsed as the Dollar rallied. Gold fell to $1,735 on the 22nd and paused before European worries reignited selling. Gold lurched down to $1,650 on the 23rd and briefly to $1,550 on the 26th on news of margin hikes in New York and Shanghai. It is now trading above $1,600. - Net long speculative positions in gold fell by 1.6 million ounces in the week to the 20th of September. This decline was due to a fall in COMEX positions which dropped from 26.8 million ounces to 25.2 million ounces. Net longs on TOCOM climbed from 1.29 million ounces to 1.31 million ounces. Unsurprisingly, long liquidation was the name of the game on COMEX. The further price falls and margin increases on COMEX and the Shanghai Gold Exchange will have driven substantial selling since that point, something that will, no doubt, be revealed in the next commitment of traders report. - Gold ETF positions fell by 76,000 ounces in the week to the 23rd of September, falling to 67.9 million ounces. Selling was seen in a few funds as the gold price fell but investor behaviour was by no means uniform with some buying seen from nervous investors. We would expect to see some further redemptions of metal in the next few days following the extended price fall. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—September 11**

- We should discuss the movements in the silver price in two different ways for the ten days from the 13th of September. Initially, the price fluctuated around the $40 mark from the 13th to the 21st. However, when the Federal Reserve revealed that QE3 was not to be (… just yet at least…) silver gave up and started plummeting. It fell in almost a strai

ght line from just over $40 on the 21st to a low of just over $26 in London trading on the 26th. (This was in contrast to silver’s price rise on speculation of QE2 in Q3 in 2010.) The dangers of taking any view on the price were soon evident though, with silver bouncing over $3 in morning trading in London before settling below $28.50. The gold:silver price ration has increased to almost 60:1 and silver investors must be worried that it could increase still further. - Silver saw almost a ten per cent decrease in net speculative long positioning on COMEX last week. It fell by 26.5 million ounces to 243.9 million ounces. This is still above the lows of market positioning seen in late June but we confidently expect the next COTR report to reveal further selling. - 2.5 million ounces of silver were sold in the week to the 23rd of September, much less than might have been expected given the sharp fall in the silver price. Almost all of the liquidation took place in the iShares fund. Total global ETF holdings of silver are now 456 million ounces, little changed from their level at the start of August. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **26 September 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 20 September 2011; ETF data to 23 September 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Once again platinum followed gold in price terms following the 23rd of September

. While a worsening economic output should have been negative for platinum, fundamentals were largely absent from the market. The impact of risk aversion could clearly be seen, though, as gold widened its premium over platinum despite its own sharp fall. Platinum slipped below $1,800 on the 19th and, in a worrying sign, failed to regain this level the following day in an unconvincing move back upwards to only $1,793. Then, gold intervened. Downgrades to Italian credit ratings and the ratings of some of the banks depressed the market and sent gold downward with platinum following. The Federal Reserve’s plans to start Operation Twist instead of QE3 sent gold lower and platinum was forced lower too. It slipped through $1,700 on the 22nd and, although it briefly regained that level on the 23rd, it fell to nearly $1,600 later that day. It lurched down to $1,480 on the 26th before bouncing to $1,560 amidst very strong Chinese purchasing. - Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX fell by over ten per cent in the week to the 20th of September to 1.89 million ounces as long liquidation and growing short positions indicated a reversal in the previously positive market sentiment. TOCOM positioning fell by 53,000 ounces to 385,000 ounces. At the point of the most recent Commitment of Traders Report, this was still a respectably bullish position held by the market. However, the slump in the price to below $1,600 will since haven driven some investors from their positions. - Platinum ETF holdings fell by 35,000 ounces in the week to the 23rd of September, dropping to 1.53 million ounces. Net selling has been seen for three of the last four weeks as even the most optimistic amongst us have started to worry about the health of global economic output. Most of the selling came from US investors who chose to reverse their buying of recent weeks. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **26 September 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 20 September 2011; ETF data to 23 September 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

- Stuttering economic growth had a negative impact on palladium prices from the middle of September onwards. Concerns over double-dip recessions and the seemingly-insoluble Euro debt crisis weighed on many assets, palladium included. The price fell back from $720 in mid-month to a low of roughly $605, a level last seen in October 2010. As with the other metals, a rising Dollar and a falling gold price overwhelmed these smaller metal markets and palladium investors cut their long positions whether through choice or necessity. The selling currently seems overdone and palladium has bounced to $640 but the immediate future for the palladium price currently seems rather uncertain. - Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX fell for a second consecutive week, and the fourth week in five, dropping 103,000 ounces to 1.05 million ounces as investors turned even more bearish on “news” of a slow global economy. In contrast to the other precious metals, open interest increased as more short positions were opened in addition to the long liquidation seen everywhere. Speculative interest now stands over 800,000 ounces lower than at the start of August as the economic environment has become more sickly. - There was more net selling from the palladium ETFs in the week to the 23rd of September. A hefty 38,500 ounces of metal were sold, with US investors having now sold 175,000 ounces of metal in recent months. Other investors remained a little more positive, with some buying seen in the various European funds. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** #### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
